content.value_statement: TypeScript library builds often need multiple formats, declarations, and clean output without slow tooling. The tsdown skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused guidance for configuring tsdown projects.
actual_capabilities: Explains tsdown installation, CLI usage, and config file setup.
Guides ESM, CJS, IIFE, and UMD output configuration.
Covers declaration generation, source maps, minification, and package exports.
Shows React, Vue, Solid, and WASM integration patterns.
Describes migration from tsup and CI-aware validation.
Covers hooks, plugins, and programmatic builds for custom workflows.
limitations: It does not install tsdown or run builds without user approval.
CSS support is documented as experimental and may change.
It cannot verify a package release unless tests and publishing are performed separately.
Examples assume working knowledge of Node.js and package managers.

use_cases.title: Create a Library Build
use_cases.description: Set up a TypeScript package with ESM, CJS, declaration files, clean output, and package exports.

use_cases.title: Migrate from tsup
use_cases.description: Translate existing tsup settings into tsdown while preserving entry points, formats, and dependency behavior.

use_cases.title: Bundle Framework Components
use_cases.description: Configure builds for React, Vue, Solid, or WASM packages with external dependencies and declaration output.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Library Build
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new package
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up tsdown for a TypeScript library with ESM, CJS, declarations, and a clean dist output. Explain each choice.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate from tsup
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current tsup setup and convert it to tsdown. Keep entry points, formats, declarations, and external dependencies equivalent.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Framework Package
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a tsdown config for a React component library. Include peer dependency externalization, declaration files, source maps, and package exports.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Release Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a tsdown-based build and validation workflow for a monorepo package. Include CI-only checks, hooks, and manual publish safeguards.

output_examples.input: I need ESM and CJS output with TypeScript declarations.
output: Recommended output formats and declaration settings.
Notes about clean output and validation before release.

output_examples.input: I am moving a package from tsup to tsdown.
output_examples.output: A migration plan that maps entry points, format options, externals, declarations, and package scripts to tsdown equivalents.

output_examples.input: My build output contains unexpected files.

best_practices: Generate declaration files for public TypeScript libraries.
Externalize peer dependencies such as React or Vue.
Use CI-only validation for package checks before publishing.
anti_patterns: Do not bundle framework peer dependencies by default.
Do not load production environment files into browser builds without filtering secrets.
Do not publish packages automatically from generated scripts without human approval.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps configure tsdown for TypeScript and JavaScript library builds, including formats, declarations, plugins, and migration work.

faq.question: Can it migrate a tsup project?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for translating common tsup settings into tsdown options.

faq.question: Does it support declaration files?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains declaration generation, declaration maps, compiler options, and related build behavior.

faq.question: Can it handle React or Vue libraries?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes framework package patterns for React, Vue, Solid, and related plugin usage.

faq.question: Will it run build or publish commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Command execution should require explicit user approval.

faq.question: Is CSS support stable in tsdown?
faq.answer: No. The included reference describes CSS support as experimental and not recommended for production reliance.
